title: Turn quanta latency/cost scratch notes
body:
Context:
Quick sketch of a small experiment we ran to explore the effect of "turn quanta" (grouping short chat turns into micro-batches) on latency percentiles and unit cost. Purpose: decide whether to include a turn-quanta option in the SDK and console as an easy knob for chat apps with short-turn interactions.

Notes / design:
- Turn quanta: accumulate up to N turns or up to T ms before dispatch (whichever hits first). Avoids per-turn RPC overhead and increases amortized KV/decoder efficiency.
- Hypothesis: for multi-turn micro-interactions (avg tokens/turn ~ 12), quanta N=3 with T=40ms reduces $/1k tokens by ~12-18% for p50-aware workloads with modest p95 uplift.
- Trade: increases tail latency for single-turn strict-latency users. Need to expose per-route policy (aggressive/conservative) and auto-detect based on session mix.

Quick ascii results (lab run, 2xA100 equiv):

Config | batching | p50 ms | p95 ms | tokens/sec | $/1k tokens
-------+---------+--------+--------+------------+--------------
Base   | none    | 48     | 220    | 480        | $0.98
Quanta-2 | N=2/T=40ms | 55     | 260    | 600        | $0.86
Quanta-3 | N=3/T=40ms | 68     | 320    | 750        | $0.79
Quanta-3+cache | N=3 + prefix KV hit 30% | 62 | 290 | 930 | $0.68

Interpretation:
- p50 increases modestly with quanta (10-40ms), but tokens/sec improves nonlinearly as more decoder work is amortized and fewer RPCs occur.
- p95 penalty is the main risk: Quanta-3 pushed p95 from 220 -> 320ms in these lab conditions. With KV cache hits (simulated 30%), the tokens/sec and $/1k swing favor quanta even more and reduce p95 impact slightly.

Mini-sparkline for throughput (relative):
Base:  ░░░░░░░░ (1.0x)
Q2:    ░░░░░░░░░░ (1.25x)
Q3:    ░░░░░░░░░░░░░ (1.56x)
Q3+K:  ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ (1.94x)

Open questions / caveats:
- Lab traffic had strong session affinity; real customer mixes will include many cold single-turn requests (in which quanta hurts). Need cohort analysis (by customer) before defaulting.
- Interaction with prefetch & tiling: if prefetch does prefix prediction we might reduce quanta benefits.
- Implementation complexity: server-side windowing vs client SDK (client-side batching avoids server scheduling complexity but requires SDK adoption).
- Fairness/SLAs: how to report SLOs when quanta is enabled? Per-request vs per-session metrics? Propose adding per-route "effective p95" that weights by session length.

Experiment plan (next 2 sprints):
1) A/B on internal traffic (alpha) - expose client flag --turn-quanta={off,naive,aggressive}. Collect per-route p50/p95 and token cost; 1 week run. Owner: Arjun.
2) Add simple worklet on runtime to expose per-session buffer occupancy metric and queue-time percentiles. Owner: Samir.
3) Produce customer cohort posterior: run analysis job on last 30d traffic to estimate potential savings per org if quanta=N in {2,3}. Output: list of top-20 orgs that would benefit. Owner: Lena.

Telemetry suggestions (what to surface in console):
- Per-route: "quanta adoption" toggle and current N/T settings.
- Quanta impact panel: p50/p95 delta, tokens/sec delta, $/1k delta, % requests delayed by >T ms due to quanta window closure.
- Session histogram: session lengths (turns) to help customers choose N.

Unresolved items (to follow up):
- Tune T: 40ms was arbitrary; try 20/40/80 ms. Add jitter to avoid synchronized flush storms.
- Decide default behavior for Dedicated vs Hosted tenants. Dedicated customers may want opt-in only.
- Security note: client-side batching implies request coalescing — ensure per-tenant isolation is preserved (no cross-tenant mixing).

Quick links / refs:
- JIRA-REQ-1287 (experiment epic)
- PR: runtime/#435 (mock quanta window)
- Slack: #serving-runtime thread "turn-quanta-pilot"

Summary (one-liner):
Turn-quanta appears promising for chat-heavy apps with short turns — meaningful cost reductions at modest p50 increases, but p95 sensitivity and mixed-traffic effects mean we should gate by route/tenant and roll out as an opt-in knob with good telemetry.
